analysis.title: Global Equity Volatility Insights: Low breadth is a feature not a bug
key_insights: S&P and Nasdaq have held up despite surging bond yields, but with historically poor breadth. Nasdaq rallied ~6% over the past month while 10y yields rose ~50bps.

US tech shows an asymmetric reaction to yields: it has rallied ~3x more on days when yields fall than on days when yields rise. Other rate-sensitive pockets lack this immunity, which adds to elevated dispersion.
BofA says low breadth is a classic feature of bubbles building and typically doesn't stop until they pop. Right-tail risk in US tech is seen as the pertinent one.
After the soft 2-Oct payroll print pushed yields lower, yields later retraced the entire move, yet the Nasdaq still closed in the green.
Realized vol on up days has far exceeded realized vol on down days in the S&P and Nasdaq over the past month, driven by US tech's upside asymmetry.

Hedge idea: QQQ call spreads, taking advantage of a historically flat call skew. QQQ Nov 40d/10d call spreads offer >4x max payout (~82nd percentile since 2012). Selling a 15d put (~8% OTM) cuts the cost of the 40d/10d call spread by ~50%.
NDX calls contingent on rates being higher but range-bound are a cheap, limited-risk way to play equities and yields trending higher together, as in recent months and the late-90s dotcom bubble.
SPX vol increasingly shows spot-up/vol-up and spot-down/vol-down behavior, especially on the call side, as the fixed-strike vol-spot beta trends toward 0.

Autocallification (growth of structured-product income issuance) is shaping vol. North American income issuance is on track for a record Q3'26 at ~$35bn pro-rated. EMEA issuance has eased from a Q1'26 peak above $40bn, and income structures are ~60% of EMEA issuance.
NVDA leads single-stock income issuance with more than $8bn YTD. MU, ORCL and GEV are running at more than 4x their 2025 pace.
SPX, SX5E, NDX and RTY trade within 2%-7% of peak Vanna from live structured products, so dealer vol-dampening flows are near their strongest.
Structured-product flows equal ~6% of daily listed vega traded in SPX, ~18% in SX5E, ~36% in NDX and up to ~185% in RTY. NDX and RTY are therefore the most autocallified benchmarks.

Fixed-strike vol-spot correlations are positive across all four indices: NDX 52.5%, SX5E 42.5%, RTY 42.3%, SPX 35.4%. Among single stocks, INTC (67.6%), AMD (64.9%), TSM (61.3%), AVGO (57.8%) and AAPL (56.7%) lead.

Trade idea: calendars that use long-dated short vol on autocallified underlyings to fund short-dated long gamma, since positioning-driven dislocations like summer 2026 can cause episodic realized-vol spikes.

The BofA GFSI rose from -0.05 on 25-Sep-26 to +0.06 on 2-Oct-26 (53rd percentile since 2000), after hitting +0.10 on Thursday, its highest since 13-Apr-26. Rates vol is now the main driver of stress, replacing commodity vol in April.

Volume flow had the largest stress increase among GFSI subcomponents (92nd percentile). USD interest-rate implied vol entered bearish territory. Euro member bond spread stress rose 99.5th percentile vs history. The GFSI Risk Allocator suggested a 2.4% underweight vs a 4.9% overweight a week earlier.

BofA Bubble Risk Indicator (BRI): US tech has the highest BRI among assets covered. Cybersecurity and US healthcare momentum baskets are at 0.93, and semis had the biggest weekly BRI jump among popular themes.
Froth in the S&P is localized vs the dotcom era: 13 S&P stocks have BRI above 0.8 vs 50-100 at the dotcom peak, and 1.8% of index weight vs 20%-40%.

BofA treats BRI above 0.8 as a rule of thumb for elevated bubble risk. High readings signal asymmetric near-term downside, with upside similar to low readings, so it is a 'watch out' tool for protection rather than a sell signal.

sector_views.rationale: BofA sees investors unwilling to lean into narrow AI/tech leadership as at risk of underperforming. It also flags bubble-like dynamics and recommends hedging upside via call spreads.
BRI levels on US healthcare stocks continue to retreat, though the healthcare momentum basket is still at 0.93.

risk_factors: Rates vol and bond-market turmoil, with global yields still climbing.
Bubble-like dynamics in the AI trade, where low breadth typically persists until the bubble pops.
Positioning-driven dislocations that cause episodic realized-vol spikes.
Rising BRI readings imply asymmetric near-term downside risk.
Peak vanna being near spot means dealer vol-dampening could fade if spot moves away from it.
charts_described: Exhibit 16 shows the Nasdaq 100 closing up on 2-Oct-26 even though the 10y yield retraced its entire soft NFP-driven move lower.
Exhibit 11 shows 13 S&P stocks with BRI above 0.8 as of 02-Oct-26, vs 50-100 at the dotcom peak.
Exhibit 12 shows 1.8% of S&P weight in stocks with BRI above 0.8, vs 20%-40% at the dotcom peak.
vol_and_positioning: Call skew is historically flat, giving a cheap entry for call spreads in S&P and Nasdaq.
Put skew is flat in SX5E and NDX, at the 7.8th and 13.4th 3y percentiles, a result partly of dealer vol supply from autocalls.
Peak vanna sits ~7% below spot in SPX, ~2% above spot in SX5E, ~3% below in NDX and ~3% below in RTY.
Peak vega for INTC, AMD, TSM, AVGO and AAPL sits ~30%-65% below spot, leaving a buffer before spot-vol correlations turn negative.
Equity-rates hybrid structures (NDX calls contingent on rates higher but range bound) are a cheap way to play the co-trend of equities and yields.
The open trades table includes long-dated upvar, NDX and SPX variance and dispersion positions, and a QQQ Oct26 730 call and an IWM Nov 280 put among others.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech optimism and AI FOMO overcome macro and policy uncertainty. US tech rallies ~3x more on yield declines than it sells off on yield rises, and the Nasdaq rose ~6% in a month despite ~50bps higher 10y yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Historically poor breadth and a high BRI are classic bubble features. High BRI readings tend to signal asymmetric near-term downside, and low breadth typically doesn't stop until the bubble pops.
